summary: This is a minimal x86-64 assembly program that sets up the data section with a hello world message and starts execution at the _start label. It moves the value 13 into the edx register, which is typically the size of the message for a system call.

explanations.2: This declares a string 'Hello, world!' followed by a newline character (0Ah). The 'db' means 'define byte' — it's telling the assembler to store these characters as raw bytes in memory.
explanations.4: The 'global' keyword exports the _start label so the operating system can find and jump to it as the program entry point.
explanations.6: This moves the number 13 into the edx register — it's counting the bytes in 'Hello, world!' plus the newline, preparing it for a write system call that will need to know how many bytes to output.
